title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study evaluating whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair, at most one repair) improves the correctness of LLM-generated network configurations relative to the single-shot initial generation. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and an automated network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (same initial generation reused for baseline and guarded). The hosted model was gpt-5-mini (temperature=null/unset). Baseline configs passed all verifier-specified invariants in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 tasks (100%), with a paired risk difference of 0.005 (95% CI 0.00–0.015), discordant pairs n10=1, n01=0, two-sided exact McNemar p=1.0. Confirmatory inference shows only a marginal absolute improvement under these task and model conditions; exploratory diagnostics show the single failure mode guarded by one repair call involved a multi-step maintenance sequence. We report preregistration, execution artifacts, and limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics) and provide reproducibility pointers in the archived execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into low-level device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Practical deployment requires that generated configurations satisfy deterministic operational invariants (reachability, policy compliance, loop-freedom, ordered-change constraints). Prior work has advocated pairing generation with verification and repair to reduce unsafe outputs, but end-to-end, verifier-backed empirical evidence in NetOps remains fragmented. We therefore preregistered and executed a paired study asking: To what extent does a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair, at most one repair) reduce invariant violations relative to a single-shot initial generation when both conditions begin from the same initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate)? Our confirmatory contribution is an empirical, fully archived paired evaluation (N=200 tasks) using a deterministic synthetic task generator, an automated network verifier, and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini). We report the preregistered analysis, exploratory failure diagnostics, and reproducibility metadata.
sections.related_work: Work on intent‑to‑configuration translation and NetOps evaluation has produced benchmarks and prototype systems that highlight the promise and risks of LLM-driven configuration synthesis [10]. The generate→validate→repair design pattern has demonstrated improved verifiability in adjacent domains (program repair, decompilation, autoregressive code generation) where execution or test oracles exist [2], [4]. Survey and safety literature emphasize LLM failure modes (hallucination/confabulation, adversarially induced fabrications) and recommend validation and provenance controls for operational use [1], [3]. Our study situates these recommendations in a controlled, verifier-centered NetOps experiment and supplies paired empirical data under shared_initial_candidate semantics so downstream claims about guarded pipelines remain precisely scoped to validator-triggered repair effects.
sections.methodology: Study design and preregistration: We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes. Design: paired binary confirmatory design comparing baseline (no repair) vs guarded (single permitted repair) per task under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Task sampling: 200 deterministic tasks generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 covering 'very_hard' and 'extreme' workflow patterns; inclusion/exclusion rules and contamination checks were fixed before model calls. Execution adapter and model: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter calling gpt-5-mini; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial generations per task = 1; maximum permitted repair calls per task = 1. Temperature field was recorded as null/unset in the model configuration; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Validation and scoring: a deterministic netops verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applied a full intent-constraint validation — syntactic parsing, per-device constraints, ordered-change/workflow policies, and network-level invariants. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion tasks with all-specified-invariants-pass). Confirmatory analysis: paired exact McNemar-style test with discordant-pair reporting, per-preregistered primary failed-call handling (complete pairs only) and prespecified sensitivity treating persistent unparsables as failures. All prompts, model calls, verifier traces, and artifacts were archived and are referenced in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution summary: run completed as preregistered (planned tasks = 200, episodes = 400). Model calls used = 201 (one extra repair-stage call). Primary confirmatory outcome: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995; 95% Wilson CI reported in archived results), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency: n11=199, n10=1 (guarded success while baseline failed), n01=0 (baseline success while guarded failed), n00=0. Estimated paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI (percentile) for the difference = [0.00, 0.015] (bootstrap resamples = 10,000). Repair activity: the guarded pipeline invoked the single permitted repair once; that repair converted the lone baseline failure into a guarded success. Exploratory diagnostics: the single repaired task involved a multi-step maintenance workflow pattern where ordering constraints spanned multiple interfaces; per-invariant breakdowns and task-level validator traces are archived. No episodes were excluded or declared unscorable per the preregistered rules.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: On this deterministic synthetic benchmark and with gpt-5-mini, single-shot LLM generation produced configurations that satisfied the verifier's specified invariants in 199/200 tasks; the guarded verifier-repair pipeline produced a marginal absolute improvement (one additional task corrected). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, the only source of per-pair difference is the verifier-triggered repair; therefore the demonstrated improvement is attributable to that repair invocation. Statistical inference: the observed discordant counts are extremely small (one discordant pair), producing a wide but near-zero-centered CI and a non-significant McNemar test (p=1.0) for this sample size and observed discordance pattern. Operational implications: deterministic verifier gates plus limited repair can address individual multi-step ordering failures, but the high baseline pass rate observed here cautions against extrapolating to production heterogeneity (vendor implementations, real telemetry, noisy state). Threats to validity: internal validity is constrained by shared_initial_candidate semantics (no independent first-pass comparisons), deterministic verifier design (oracle correctness), and single-model testing. Construct validity: the verifier operationalizes correctness in terms of syntactic parse, per-device constraints, and encoded workflow policies but may omit aspects of runtime semantics observable only on live devices. External validity: tasks are synthetic and topologies are controlled; only gpt-5-mini was tested. Conclusion validity: with only one discordant pair, the study is underpowered to demonstrate small absolute improvements beyond the observed marginal effect; the experiment nonetheless documents an operationally realistic pipeline and full execution artifacts for reproducibility.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation of verifier-guarded configuration synthesis using a hosted LLM under shared_initial_candidate semantics. In this deterministic synthetic task corpus, single-shot generation already produced nearly complete verifier compliance (199/200). A single verifier-triggered repair converted the single failing case into success, yielding a small absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points). These results show that verifier-based repair can remediate specific multi-step ordering failures, but do not by themselves establish broad production benefits. Future work should evaluate multiple models, larger and more diverse task banks (including noisy/partial state and live-device execution), independent first-pass comparisons (when permitted by execution semantics), adversarial retrieval/poisoning scenarios, and richer runtime oracles that capture dynamic device semantics. All experimental artifacts and analysis outputs are archived in the execution manifest referenced below to support reproducibility and follow-up studies.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This study was executed under CNSM Agentic-AI Researcher track rules and preregistration CAND-2026-001. The hosted model used was gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution manifest). The experiment adapter and orchestration framework were hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (adapter family). The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba (immutable archived reference). The Research Director defined the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained scope prior to the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock all literature review, experiment selection, preregistration, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, peer review, and revision were performed autonomously. The preregistered plan required generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial generation per task was sampled and reused across baseline and guarded conditions; therefore the paired difference arises only from verifier-triggered repair. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair call per task; in this run one repair call occurred (recorded in the execution manifest). The model configuration recorded temperature=null/unset — null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All runtime artifacts (prompts, model outputs, provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, analysis artifacts, and execution manifest) are archived as stated in the execution_manifest and are available per the track's artifact policy. Pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were not used as empirical evidence for this final run; only artifacts produced under the preregistered post-lock execution are reported as results.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and the deterministic verifier; they do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent prompt-engineering or constrained-generation effects.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
